name: Conway Corp
old_description: Our commitment to the community where we work and live is the reason we were founded. We remain dedicated to enhancing the quality of life in our community through our services, education initiatives and economic development involvement.
about:
Conway Corp has operated from Conway, Arkansas since 1929, when city leaders signed a charter on May 6 to create the Conway Corporation. The municipal utility was formed to take over the city's electric light plant and, by 1930, its waterworks and sewer plant. It remains a city-owned, nonprofit corporation governed by a local board, with a mission to enhance quality of life through utility and telecommunications services.

The corporation provides electric, water, wastewater, video, internet, voice, and security services to residential and business customers across the Conway area. Its infrastructure includes the Stone Dam Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant, the James H. Brewer Lake reservoir, the Gleason Water Treatment Plant, multiple electric substations, and a fiber-coax hybrid cable network upgraded in the 1990s. Crews operate 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, and the company launched one of the earliest broadband cable internet services in the country in 1997.

Customers range from individual households to local businesses and the broader Conway community. The utility serves the city's residential neighborhoods, commercial districts, and a designated Data District where gigabit internet was first rolled out to businesses. It also supports economic development initiatives and education programs as part of its community mandate.

The company states it was founded on a commitment to the community where its employees live and work. Its core values — customer satisfaction, innovation, safety, reliability, responsibility, and community — are framed as the reason it exists, with a focus on delivering safe, affordable, and environmentally sound services while maintaining fiscal stewardship.
